module.purpose: Provides authentication email verification workflows, including feature gating, watchlist blocking, rate limiting, token persistence, time-based code generation, localization, and delivery of verification messages.
module.summary: This module supports verification of primary, secondary, and changed email addresses. It generates expiring database-backed tokens for link verification, derives time-based verification codes for code-based verification, applies feature and abuse-prevention checks, and delegates localized email delivery to the email manager. Platform-specific requests can bypass link delivery, while blocked addresses are refused.
module.businessContext:
Supports account security and email ownership confirmation in the authentication system.
Failures can prevent sign-up, email changes, or secondary-address verification, while bypassing controls could enable abuse.

detail.name: sendEmailVerification
detail.signature: async ({ email, language, username, secondaryEmailId, isPlatform = false }: VerifyEmailType) => Promise<{ ok: boolean; skipped: boolean }>
preconditions: The caller provides an object conforming to VerifyEmailType.
If a language is not supplied, "en" will be used as default.
postconditions: If the feature is disabled or the request is for a platform account, the function returns { ok: true, skipped: true } without creating a token or sending an email.
If the email is blocked, the function returns { ok: false, skipped: false } without creating a token or sending an email.
Otherwise a verification token is persisted, an email verification link is sent, and the function returns { ok: true, skipped: false }.
invariants: When a token is created, it is a 64‑character hexadecimal string.
edgeCases: Email present in watch‑list → returns ok false.
isPlatform flag true → returns skipped true.

raises: Error from checkRateLimitAndThrowError or any unhandled exception

stateMutations: Potential DB reads via FeaturesRepository and watch‑list check
detail.summary: Sends an email verification link if the email‑verification feature is enabled, the email is not blocked, and the request is not for a platform account, respecting rate limits.

detail.name: sendChangeOfEmailVerification
detail.signature: export const sendChangeOfEmailVerification = async ({ user, language }: ChangeOfEmail) =>
preconditions: The input conforms to ChangeOfEmail and provides a user with emailFrom, emailTo, and username values.
Configured dependencies for translation, feature lookup, rate limiting, persistence, watchlist checking, and email delivery are available.
postconditions: If global email verification is disabled, no token is persisted or email sent and the result is { ok: true, skipped: true }.
If the source email is blocked, no rate-limit check, token persistence, or email send occurs and the result is { ok: false, skipped: false }.

Otherwise, a verification token associated with user.emailFrom and expiring 24 hours after creation is persisted, a verification link is sent to user.emailTo, and the result is { ok: true, skipped: false }.
invariants: The generated token is produced from 32 random bytes and encoded as a hexadecimal string.
The rate-limit identifier is the hash of user.emailFrom.
The verification link contains the generated token as the token query parameter.
The persisted token identifier is user.emailFrom.
edgeCases: When language is nullish, translation lookup uses the en language and common namespace.
When global email verification is disabled, the function returns successfully with skipped true.
When user.emailFrom is on the blocked watchlist, the function returns with ok false and skipped false without sending an email.
If rate limiting, token persistence, translation, watchlist checking, feature lookup, or email delivery fails, the resulting error is propagated and no success result is returned.

raises: Errors from translation lookup, feature lookup, watchlist checking, rate-limit enforcement, verification-token persistence, or email delivery are propagated.
errorPolicy.returnsOnError: { ok: false, skipped: false } only when the source email is blocked; other errors are thrown.

stateMutations: Creates a verificationToken database record with identifier user.emailFrom, the generated hexadecimal token, and an expiration 24 hours from creation.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns a Promise resolving to either { ok: true, skipped: true } when disabled, { ok: false, skipped: false } when blocked, or { ok: true, skipped: false } after sending. The sent URL has the form WEBAPP_URL + /auth/verify-email-change?token=<hexadecimal-token>. The persisted verificationToken data has identifier, token, and expires fields.
detail.summary: Creates a verification token and sends a change-of-email verification link unless email verification is disabled or the source email is blocked. It enforces rate limiting before persisting the token and sending the link.

specTests.then: It resolves to { ok: true, skipped: true } and does not persist a token or send a verification email.
It resolves to { ok: false, skipped: false } without performing rate limiting, token persistence, or email delivery.

It rate-limits using hashEmail(user.emailFrom), persists a hexadecimal token for user.emailFrom expiring in 24 hours, sends a link containing that token to user.emailTo, and resolves to { ok: true, skipped: false }.
